fields.meta_title: Audit Workflow: Requests, Tests, and Findings | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an audit workflow that assigns evidence requests, records sample tests and store inspections, and escalates findings that run late.
fields.h1: Build an Audit Workflow That Gives Every Item an Owner
fields.hero_description: Build an audit workflow that assigns each request and finding to an owner and keeps the record in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: The Parts of an Audit Workflow Emergent Builds
fields.features_subheading: Each part keeps an audit item moving: who owns it, when it is due, and where its evidence lives.
fields.feature_1:
An owner and a due date on every request

Load the request list once, and each line gets one named owner and a due date. Owners upload files against their own lines, and the audit lead sees every line and its status.
fields.feature_2:
Reminders that turn into escalations

Pick when a reminder goes out in Slack or by email, and how many days late an item can run before the owner's manager hears about it. Nobody keeps a chase list by hand.
fields.feature_3:
Evidence saved with the item it answers

Each uploaded file is stored with the request or test it answers and the person who sent it. The record sits in a database you own, and next year's audit can start from it.
fields.feature_4:
AI reads statements and invoices

An AI step turns uploaded bank statements, invoices, and receipts into fields such as the amount and the payee. A person confirms any value the AI is unsure of before testing.
fields.feature_5:
One live board for the whole audit

The dashboard lists open requests and findings by owner, with late items pinned to the top. It updates as files arrive, and status meetings start from the same numbers.
fields.feature_6:
Your audit app's code, in your GitHub

Export the audit app's full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Your IT team can review how evidence is stored and who can open it, the same way they review other code.

fields.tab_content_1:
Bank reconciliations 3 days late go to the controller

Harrowgate Tile Supply's external auditors send 38 year-end requests, and 31 are delivered. Request 17, the March bank reconciliations, belongs to Lucan Mensforth, who got a reminder on the due date. Any request 3 days late goes to the controller, and Perpetua Valdesuso now has a direct message naming it.
fields.tab_content_2:
Two exceptions in the sample open a finding

Rafferty Nwachukwu tests the expense approval control at Kettlewick Freight on 25 sampled expense reports. Of the 25, 23 pass. The other two were approved after payment, and any exception opens a finding. Finding F-07 goes to Hesper Ostrowe, the AP manager, for her response.
fields.tab_content_3:
Store 4 gets 7 days to fix one failed item

Soraya Pendleford inspects store 4 of Fernhollow Bakehouse on her phone against a 40-item checklist, and every fail needs a photo. Store 4 passes 39 of 40: the walk-in cooler log has unsigned entries. The store manager, Bertil Achebe, gets a corrective action due in 7 days by direct message, with the photo.
fields.tab_content_4:
Overdue finding F-11 lands with the CFO

Pellacombe Dental Group tracks 12 findings from last year's audit, and only the auditor can close one. Nine are closed, two are open on time, and one is overdue. F-11, a shared login on the billing system owned by Ottoline Brachvogel, is 10 days overdue. Any finding over 7 days overdue goes to the CFO by direct message.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an Audit Workflow
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to turn last year's audit into an audit workflow with owners, deadlines, and evidence, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the audits you support each year
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Start from last year's request list
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Pick the reminder and escalation days
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Connect the ledger and file storage
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every audit your team supports in a year: the external year-end audit, internal control tests, store or site inspections, and any customer review. Next to each, note who sends requests, who answers them, and where the files go today. Start with the audit that needs the most chasing.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open last year's PBC list, the documents and information the auditor requested from you, instead of a blank page. Keep its numbering, put a named person and a deadline on each line, and mark repeat requests. Describe the list and its rules in a prompt, and Emergent builds the tracker.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose two numbers for every item: the day a reminder goes to its owner, and how many days past due it can go before it moves up to the owner's manager. Set them per audit, because a year-end request and a store inspection run on different clocks.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect your accounting system and file storage through their APIs, such as QuickBooks, Xero, or NetSuite. A request for reconciliations or invoices can then pull the source record, and the tester compares it with the uploaded file instead of retyping figures.
fields.howto_step_5_des: List what every finding must carry before it can close: an owner, a due date, the owner's written response, and evidence of the fix. Name the person who reviews that evidence, and keep closed findings on file for next year's follow-up review.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Rerun last year's audit through the app before the next one starts. Load 10 requests you already answered with their files, and leave one late on purpose to confirm the reminder and the escalation both arrive. Fix any rule by prompting, then run it again.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live on a fixed-date audit
fields.howto_step_7_des: Pick an audit with a fixed date for the first live run, such as the year-end requests. Tell owners where their requests now live, watch the first escalations closely, and adjust the reminder days after a month. Move the next audit over once owners stop asking for the spreadsheet.
fields.hero_prompt: Build an audit workflow that runs on its own and logs every step.

faq_plan.a: An audit workflow is the ordered set of steps an audit follows, with a person and a deadline attached to each one. A typical audit has four stages: planning, fieldwork, reporting, and follow-up. The workflow is the work inside those stages: each request answered and each finding closed.

faq_plan.q: How to design efficient audit workflow processes?
faq_plan.ref: how to design efficient audit workflow processes
faq_plan.a: Design it around the items that move, not the calendar. Give every item one owner, one due date, and one place for its evidence. Then set the day each reminder goes out and the day a late item escalates. Reuse last year's list as the starting point. In Emergent's AI automation builder, you write those rules in plain English and get a working app.

faq_plan.q: How to automate audit workflow and task assignments?
faq_plan.ref: how to automate audit workflow and task assignments
faq_plan.a: Assign by rule instead of by email. Map each request type or control to a role, such as bank reconciliations to the AP lead, and have the app create every task with its due date when the audit opens. When someone changes jobs, you update one mapping. Emergent builds that assignment logic from a plain-English prompt.

faq_plan.q: How to automate compliance and audit workflows?
faq_plan.ref: how to automate compliance and audit workflows
faq_plan.a: Automate the controls first, then the audit of them. When approvals and reconciliations already run in software, each one leaves a dated record, and the audit becomes pulling records instead of chasing emails. Purchase order automation is one place to start: each order's approver and amount are logged when the order is placed.

faq_plan.q: How digital platforms simplify audit workflows?
faq_plan.ref: how digital platforms simplify audit workflows
faq_plan.a: They replace the shared spreadsheet and the email chain with one record per item that holds its owner and its files. Reminders go out on schedule, and the auditor sees what is late without a status call. When you compare audit workflow tools, check that the record carries over into next year's audit.

faq_plan.q: How to automate data extraction in audit workflows?
faq_plan.ref: how to automate data extraction in audit workflows
faq_plan.a: Use an AI step that reads each document into fields, starting with documents that arrive in volume and share a layout, such as bank statements and vendor invoices. Match those fields against the ledger and show the tester only the differences. Apps built with Emergent can include that reading step and pull the ledger side through an API.

faq_plan.q: How do you implement a paperless audit workflow?
faq_plan.ref: how to implement paperless audit workflow
faq_plan.a: Pick one place for every file, then stop accepting evidence by email or on paper. Scan paper records once, at the source, and name each scan by its request number. Record approvals as a dated click in the app instead of initials on a printout. For letters your team sends, such as bank confirmation requests, document automation can fill them from a template.

faq_plan.q: How can a team improve audit workflow collaboration?
faq_plan.ref: how to improve audit workflow collaboration
faq_plan.a: Work from one shared list instead of separate trackers. Let auditors and request owners see the same status for each item, and keep questions as comments on the item rather than in email threads, where the next person can read them. Hold one short weekly review of late items only, and name who acts on each one before the call ends.

faq_plan.q: How to use ai to speed up audit workflows?
faq_plan.ref: how to use ai to speed up audit workflows
faq_plan.a: Use AI where the work is reading and writing, and keep the judgment with the auditor. Three tasks suit it: drafting a finding from the tester's notes, summarizing a long management response, and comparing this year's findings with last year's to spot repeats. Have a person review each draft before it goes into the report.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in audit workflow software?
faq_plan.a: Look first at who you pay for. Request owners outside finance may answer two items a year, and per-user pricing charges for each of them. Then confirm you can export every file and decision when the audit ends. Emergent builds the app on a database you own, with full code export on paid plans.
